title: ASMR / start-page filming guide
question: Can Omni produce a ~10s vertical phone loop that teaches slow pan + spoken room name, grounded on an accepted kitchen still, suitable as a local start-page demo?
one_way_note: This clip is not scored for item recall and cannot inform capture-strategy or accuracy claims. It is a product-surface demo asset. Label it synthetic in the UI if shown.
operator_notes: If speech is wrong or music appears, reject — audio mode is part of the acceptance criteria.
Do not drop into the VU tasks queue; stage under video/exploratory/outputs/ if kept.
docs/17 asked for a silent loop; this variant adds one spoken room name on purpose (speaking-capture hypothesis). For a silent sibling, strip audio with ffmpeg — same footage, zero extra Omni quota.
wall: Demo / development only. Never present as a real landlord walkthrough. Google terms: internal use.

audio.voice: calm British adult, plain and unhurried
audio.after_cue: silence for the rest of the clip; no music, no footsteps, no ambient room tone

intended_negatives: clean timber grain is not mould
clips.exact_prompt: Create one continuous photorealistic video that looks like an ordinary handheld smartphone walkthrough of a kitchen in a recently refurbished compact UK terrace with inexpensive white fittings. The supplied reference image is the opening frame: match its layout, fittings, finishes and lighting exactly, then move from it. Camera: hold the reference framing for about one second, then pan slowly left to right across the kitchen at the pace of a careful landlord filming evidence; pause briefly when the sink and worktop edge are centred; small natural handheld wobble only; vertical phone framing throughout. One unbroken take from a single handheld phone. Visible evidence required across the take: white kitchen units, oak-effect worktop, sink, oven, ceramic hob. Intended visible defects: none. Negative controls: clean timber grain is not mould. The room is clean and tidy with clear worktops under bright overcast daylight. Hold fixed for the whole take: same white shaker units, oak-effect worktop, black appliances and rear window. Audio: one line of speech only, calm British adult, plain and unhurried, saying exactly "Kitchen" at about 1.5 seconds in; then silence for the rest of the clip; no music, no footsteps, no ambient room tone. Avoid: people, logos, readable text, watermark, impossible geometry, scene cuts, dissolves or fades, speed ramps, slow motion, title cards, music, sound effects, camera-operator commentary, drone or crane moves, tripod-smooth motorised motion. Do not add labels, captions, borders, or inspection annotations. Show only visually supportable property evidence; do not make hidden areas visible.
acceptance_extra: pace reads as careful evidence filming, not a cinematic drone

sketch_variant.note: Optional second slot: photograph a hand-drawn shot list (wide box → arrow → detail box → pause mark) and use Omni's drawing-as-motion-guide path. Do not show the drawing in the final video. Same kitchen evidence contract as EX-4 if you also attach RP-003-A-wide; otherwise treat as pure UX metaphor and do not score.
sketch_variant.exact_prompt: Turn this drawing into realistic vertical smartphone footage of a careful landlord filming a kitchen inventory, using the drawing only as a guide for camera movement; do not show the drawing in the final video. Slow left-to-right pan, brief pause on a sink and worktop edge, small handheld wobble, 9:16. One unbroken take. Audio: one calm British voice saying exactly "Kitchen" at about 1.5 seconds, then silence. No people faces, no logos, no readable brand text, no music, no titles.
